pp:ee:2024:q26.title: GATE EE 2024 | Set 1 | Question: 26
pp:ee:2024:q26.question: Consider a vector $\bar{u}=2 \hat{x}+\hat{y}+2 \hat{z}$, where $\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z}$ represent unit vector along the coordinate axes $x, y, z$ respectively. The directional derivative of the function $f(x, y, z)=2 \ln (x y)+\ln (y z)+3 \ln (x z)$ at the point $(x, y, z)=(1,1,1)$ in the direction of $\bar{u}$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:
We know that: directional derivative of '$f$' at $P(1,1,1)$ in the direction of $\vec{a}$ is given by

$$\begin{aligned}

\text { Directional derivative } & =\nabla f \cdot \frac{\hat{a}}{|\bar{a}|} \\

\nabla f & =\hat{i} \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}+\hat{j} \frac{\partial f}{\partial y}+\hat{k} \frac{\partial f}{\partial z} \\

\nabla f & =i \frac{5}{x}+j \frac{3}{y}+k \frac{4}{z} \\

(\nabla f)_{(1,1,1)} & =5 i+3 j+4 k

\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ Directional derivative $=\overline{\nabla f} \cdot \frac{\bar{a}}{|\bar{a}|}=(5 i+3 j+4 k) \cdot \frac{(2 i+j+2 k)}{\sqrt{2^{2}+1^{2}+2^{2}}}=\frac{21}{3}=7$

pp:ee:2024:q27.title: GATE EE 2024 | Set 1 | Question: 27
pp:ee:2024:q27.question:
The input $x(t)$ and the output $y(t)$ of a system are related as

$y(t)=e^{-t} \int_{-\infty}^{t} e^{\tau} x(\tau) d \tau, \quad-\infty \lt t \lt \infty$

The system is

detailed_solution.concept: Signals and Systems - Linear Time Invariant Systems
detailed_solution.markdown:
System will follow law of superposition. Therefore, system will be linear.

Time-invariance check:

$y\left(t-t_{0}\right)=e^{-\left(t-t_{0}\right)} \int_{-\infty}^{t-t_{0}} e^{\tau} \cdot x(\tau) d \tau$

For input $x\left(t-t_{0}\right)$, output will be

$y(t)=e^{-t} \int_{-\infty}^{t} e^{\tau} \cdot x\left(\tau-t_{0}\right) d \tau$

Put $\tau-t_{o}=k$, then $d \tau=d k$ and for $\tau=t, k=t-t_{0}$

$$\begin{aligned}

& =e^{-t} \int_{-\infty}^{t-t_{0}} e^{k+t_{0}} \cdot x(k) d k \\

& =e^{-t} \times e^{t o} \times \int_{-\infty}^{t-t_{0}} e^{k} \cdot x(k) d k=e^{-\left(t-t_{0}\right)} \times \int_{-\infty}^{t-t_{0}} e^{k} \cdot x(k) d k \\

& =e^{-\left(t-t_{0}\right)} \times \int_{-\infty}^{t-t_{0}} e^{\tau} \cdot x(\tau) d \tau

\end{aligned}$$

Since,

$y(t)=y\left(t-t_{0}\right)$

So, the system is time-invariant.

pp:ee:2024:q28.title: GATE EE 2024 | Set 1 | Question: 28
pp:ee:2024:q28.question:
Consider the discrete-time system $T_{1}$ and $T_{2}$ defined as follows:

$$\begin{aligned} & \left\{T_{1} x\right\}[n]=x[0]+x[1]+\ldots+x[n] \\ & \left\{T_{2} x\right\}[n]=x[0]+\frac{1}{2} x[1]+\cdots+\frac{1}{2^{n}} x[n] \end{aligned}$$

Which one of the following statement is true?
options: $T_{1}$ is BIBO stable but $T_{2}$ is not BIBO stable.
$T_{1}$ is not BIBO stable but $T_{2}$ is BIBO stable.

primary.subtopicLabel: Introduction of C.T. and D.T. Signals

detailed_solution.concept: Signals and Systems - Introduction of C.T. and D.T. Signals
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned}

\left\{T_{1} x\right\}[n] & =x[0]+x[1]+\ldots+x[n] \\

\left\{T_{1} x\right\}[n]^{-} & =\sum_{K=0}^{n} x[K]

\end{aligned}$$

Let,

$$\begin{aligned}

x[K] & =u[K] \\

\mid x[K] & =|u[K]| \\

\left|\left\{T_{1} x\right\}[n]\right| & =\left|\sum_{K=0}^{n} u[K]\right|=\sum_{K=0}^{n} 1=n

\end{aligned}$$

$\mid\left[\left.T_{1} x(n)\right|_{n=\infty}=\infty\right.$ system is not BIBO stable

$$\begin{aligned}

\left\{T_{2} x\right\}[n] & =x[0]+\frac{1}{2} x[1]+\cdots+\frac{1}{2^{n}} x[n] \\

& =\sum_{K=0}^{n}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{K} x(K)

\end{aligned}$$

Let,

$$\begin{aligned}

x(K) & =u[K] \\

|x[K]| & =\mid u[K] \\

\left\{T_{2} x\right\}[n] & =\sum_{K=0}^{n}\left|\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{K} u(K)\right| \\

\left\{T_{2} x\right\}[n] & =\sum_{K=0}^{n}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{K} \\

\mid\left[\left.T_{2} x(n)\right|_{n=\infty}\right. & =\sum_{K=0}^{\infty}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{K}=\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{2}}=2 \text { stable }

\end{aligned}$$

$T_{1}$ is not BIBO stable but $T_{2}$ is $\mathrm{BIBO}$ stable.

detailed_solution.markdown: Rating of DC machine 210 V, 10 A, 1200 rpm, $$\begin{aligned} & R_{a}=1 \Omega \\ & I_{F} \rightarrow \text { constant } \\ & \therefore \quad \phi \rightarrow \text { constant } \\ & \therefore \quad E_{b}=K_{m} W=K_{m} \cdot \frac{2 \pi \cdot N}{60} \\ & V_{0}=E_{b}+I_{0} R_{a} \\ & 210=K_{m} \cdot \frac{2 \pi N}{60}+I_{0} R_{a} \\ & 210=K_{m} \cdot \frac{2 \pi \cdot 1200}{60}+(10 \times 1) \\ & K_{m}=1.59(\mathrm{~V}-\mathrm{s}) / \mathrm{rad} \end{aligned}$$ Armature terminals reversed $\therefore \quad E_{b} \rightarrow$ Negative Inv for regenerative braking $$\begin{aligned} V_{0} & =-E_{b}+I_{0} R_{a} \\ \frac{2 V_{m}}{\pi} \cos \alpha & =-E_{b}+I_{0} R_{a} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} \frac{2.240 \sqrt{2}}{\pi} \cos \alpha & =-K_{m} \cdot \frac{2 \pi N}{60}+I_{0} R_{a} \\ \frac{2 \cdot 240 \sqrt{2}}{\pi} \cdot \cos \alpha & =-1.59\left(\frac{2 \pi \cdot 600}{60}\right)+10 \\ \alpha & =114.58^{\circ} \end{aligned}$$
